title: Local credit assignment that matches backpropagation at scale

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a learning rule that lets each part of a deep network determine how to change its own connections using information available locally in space and time, while matching the learning performance of strong backpropagation baselines. Credit assignment means determining which internal changes would improve the network’s overall task performance. The central challenge is to make useful intermediate features emerge without sending task-error derivatives backward through the entire network.

The target includes sustained performance as network depth, model size and training data increase. A local objective that works on a small classification problem would be a partial demonstration; the intended advance requires competitive feature learning across demanding tasks and multiple scales. Locality also needs an operational definition: local elementary computations can still participate in an iterative process whose useful result depends on convergence across the network.

Scope synthesis: this entry concerns algorithmic parity without an end-to-end backward pass. It does not require the rule to surpass backpropagation in accuracy, speed or stability, and it does not assume that locality automatically produces inexpensive hardware or biological-order power consumption. Hardware implementation and energy efficiency are additional demonstrations with their own requirements.

significance.text: Backpropagation is a standard method for training deep networks. It carries task-error derivatives backward through successive layers, and conventional implementations retain forward activations for that computation. Those dependencies create memory and scheduling burdens. Matching its learning performance with local updates would remove a major coordination requirement from training while preserving the ability to learn useful internal representations.

The direct consequence would be comparable learning within the demonstrated task and scale range without a global backward sweep. Reduced dependencies between layer updates could support pipelined or asynchronous training. Hinton’s Forward-Forward discussion motivates processing sequential data without retaining neural activities for later error propagation, but the practical scheduling and throughput advantages of a competitive large-scale rule would still need measurement.

Analog, spiking and in-memory implementations are conditional downstream opportunities. A rule that uses locally available signals could be easier to map onto such substrates, especially where storing activities or computing precise backward derivatives is difficult. Locality alone does not establish compatibility, numerical robustness or an energy advantage. The supplied material describes practical difficulties with analog backpropagation; it does not show that backpropagation logically requires synchronous digital hardware.

Impact synthesis: passing the proposed billion-parameter language-modeling milestone would demonstrate parity within that suite, rather than establish frontier-quality learning in general. Frontier relevance would require appropriate capabilities, scales and baselines. Consumer-hardware training, superiority over backpropagation and the biological-order power goal of MLC-11 remain separate claims. Biological inspiration motivates the search for local rules but does not establish that an artificial implementation will reproduce the brain’s efficiency.

missing_breakthrough.text: The missing capability is a rule that combines spatially and temporally local credit assignment with strong feature learning, and preserves that combination as depth and training scale grow. The scientific difficulty is making locally useful changes align with the final task objective: improving a layer’s own objective need not produce representations that later layers can use as effectively as representations trained end to end. The supplied experiments document substantial gaps for several tested local objectives, without establishing an impossibility result for arbitrary local learning rules.

Predictive coding illustrates an important distinction between local operations and network-wide dependencies. The supplied discussion describes approaches that recover the backpropagation gradient at a fixed point of iterative inference. It also describes an implemented cheaper variant that removes the inference loop and becomes local supervised learning. Recovering the desired gradient therefore does not, by itself, demonstrate removal of the coordination or convergence burden. Conversely, an iterative method should not be called nonlocal merely because it iterates: its operations, communication dependencies and stopping conditions must be specified.

Temporal locality creates a related engineering challenge. A rule must specify how much past activity it retains, how long information must remain available and whether delayed task feedback requires reconstructing earlier computations. The supplement to Backpropagation and the brain discusses the storage demands of backpropagation through time, while Forward-Forward motivates avoiding activity retention for later error propagation. Avoiding the full backward activation graph is meaningful, but a complete implementation must also disclose other retained state and delayed dependencies.

Engineering synthesis: a convincing solution must make its information flow explicit and maintain competitive learning under realistic training and tuning budgets. If iterative inference, auxiliary objectives or additional passes are required, their costs must be measured. The supplied evidence does not establish that predictive-coding inference necessarily costs as much as backpropagation, nor that every local approach must encounter the gaps reported for the tested methods.

current_state.text: On 17 April 2020, Lillicrap, Santoro, Marris, Akerman and Hinton published Backpropagation and the brain in Nature Reviews Neuroscience, volume 21, pages 335–346. Its available abstract discusses the biological difficulties associated with backpropagation and how feedback-induced activity changes might approximate learning signals. This is a conceptual account of possible mechanisms, not a demonstration of an artificial local rule matching backpropagation at large scale. The supplied review had a subscription preview of the main article and a complete supplement; access to the supplement does not imply access to the full main article.

Hinton’s Forward-Forward algorithm, posted to arXiv on 27 December 2022, replaces the conventional forward-and-backward training sequence with two forward passes. The supplied review covered the complete 16-page paper. Its demonstrations concern small problems, and its discussion explicitly leaves large-network scaling unresolved. It establishes a concrete alternative learning mechanism and motivates potential hardware benefits, but does not demonstrate large-scale parity. It is presented here as an arXiv preprint; the supplied record does not establish a subsequent publication outcome.

Wu, Liu and Chen’s The Price of Locality, supplied as arXiv version 1 dated 27 September 2026, reports substantial performance gaps for tested local methods. On CIFAR-10 ResNets, backpropagation accuracy remained approximately 0.95–0.96, supervised local methods trailed by about 5–8 percentage points, and goodness-based Forward-Forward accuracy was approximately 0.31–0.42. The paper reports that the Forward-Forward gap worsened with depth within its experiments. These are attributed preprint results over the tested configurations, rather than a general theorem about local learning.

For OpenWebText language-model training, the same preprint reports that the NCE-to-backpropagation perplexity ratio increased from 3.73 to 9.19 across its tested scales, while the LCE-to-backpropagation ratio increased from 1.20 to 1.51. Lower perplexity is better, so these ratios indicate worsening relative performance for those methods. The largest reported model had 124 million parameters and a 2.48-billion-token training budget; its backpropagation baseline reached perplexity 28. The prose identifies the 9.19 ratio as NCE versus backpropagation even though Table 2 abbreviates the relevant column as FFA. It should therefore not be represented as a vanilla Forward-Forward result.

The supplied review retained the preprint’s relevant results prose and Table 2, including all five scale rows, but the extraction was truncated during Appendix B.4. Figure 2 itself and the later experimental appendices were not inspected. The numerical summary is supported by the retained prose and table, while full assessment of the experimental procedures remains limited by that coverage. The reported deterioration occurs within a range that does not establish frontier-scale behavior; extrapolation beyond that range remains uncertain.

Evidence-bound synthesis: the supplied work establishes concrete local-learning approaches and reported shortcomings of several tested methods. It does not demonstrate the target innovation, prove that no other rule can achieve it, or establish a comprehensive present-day absence of solutions. No freshness search record was supplied, so field-wide openness as of the review’s 1 November 2026 cutoff remains unresolved. That limitation is not evidence that the reported results are false.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed algorithmic milestone: on a preregistered language-modeling suite, demonstrate a local rule with a perplexity ratio no greater than 1.1 relative to a strong backpropagation baseline at one billion parameters or more. The implementation must neither retain the full forward activation graph for a backward pass nor propagate task error backward through all downstream layers. The ratio and size threshold are proposed choices for this record, not established community standards.
completion_criteria.label: Local rule reaches ≤1.1× backpropagation perplexity at ≥1 billion parameters

completion_criteria.text: Proposed scaling protocol: test several model sizes, depths and training-data budgets, including the qualifying billion-parameter setting. Preregister baseline selection, architecture comparisons, data, training and tuning budgets, evaluation procedures and statistical reporting. Report absolute perplexities alongside ratios and disclose all auxiliary training work. One successful model would establish a milestone at that setting; sustained parity requires evidence across the scaling sequence, and broader feature-learning claims require additional demanding tasks.
completion_criteria.label: Preregister scaling comparisons and report perplexities with auxiliary training work

completion_criteria.text: Proposed locality and reproducibility checks: document the information available to each update, temporal retention windows, communication paths, synchronization requirements and any iterative inference. Release sufficient code, configurations and evaluation details for independent reproduction, including variability across repeated runs. Measure activation and other state storage, computation and communication so that a hidden network-wide dependency or expensive inference loop cannot be mistaken for removal of the original burden. Finite tests would establish demonstrated breadth, not literal universality across tasks or architectures.
completion_criteria.label: Document reproducible update locality and measure full resource costs

completion_criteria.text: Proposed separate hardware milestone: implement the same rule on a non-digital or in-memory substrate and report measured training energy per token together with achieved learning quality. Define the accounting boundary, including host computation, data movement and any digital auxiliary or gradient calculations. Algorithmic parity may be demonstrated before this hardware milestone. The hardware result would characterize that implementation and would not alone establish frontier competence at a biological-order power budget under MLC-11.
completion_criteria.label: Report non-digital or in-memory training energy per token and quality

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: MLC-01, A predictive theory of what deep networks learn, could help explain when a local objective produces useful representations or fails as depth grows. MLC-05 instead requires an effective learning mechanism; predictive understanding and a working local rule are distinct achievements.

Roster-based synthesis: MLC-02, Domain learning at a human experience budget, concerns learning from limited experience, whereas MLC-05 concerns how credit reaches internal parameters. MLC-03, Cumulative learning without forgetting or loss of plasticity, concerns retaining and extending competence over time. Local updates could be investigated in both settings, but locality alone establishes neither sample efficiency nor resistance to forgetting.

Roster-based synthesis: MLC-04, World models that survive novel interventions, concerns the robustness of learned models under interventions. A local rule might train such a model, but matching backpropagation on a training suite would not establish intervention robustness. MLC-06, Algorithmic legibility sufficient to verify and edit a model, concerns understanding and modifying the resulting computation; locally generated updates do not necessarily make learned representations legible.

Roster-based synthesis: MLC-07, Open-ended curricula that create externally verified new competencies, concerns the generation and validation of learning experiences. MLC-08, Discovery of new empirical laws, confirmed by experiment, concerns scientifically validated outputs. A local credit-assignment rule could support systems pursuing either goal, while its own parity demonstration would establish neither open-ended competence growth nor empirical discovery.

Roster-based synthesis: MLC-09, Skill learning from scarce, irreversible, real-world outcomes, adds constraints on data collection and delayed consequences that could make temporal credit assignment especially relevant. Its real-world learning requirements remain separate from language-modeling parity. MLC-10, Non-vacuous behavioral certificates at frontier scale, concerns justified behavioral guarantees; reproducible training performance under MLC-05 is not itself such a certificate.

Roster-based synthesis: MLC-11, Frontier competence at a biological-order power budget, has the closest hardware overlap. MLC-05 asks whether local learning can match backpropagation as scale grows; MLC-11 asks for a competence-and-power outcome. A local rule could contribute to that outcome, but a GPU implementation or an isolated energy-per-token result would not establish it. The roster supplies MLC-11’s title but no detailed criteria, so the precise accounting boundary and required competence cannot be inferred here.

brief.title: AI training with each layer learning locally
possible: Researchers could train large AI models with each layer learning from nearby information available at the time, while matching strong standard training methods. Today’s standard, backpropagation, sends error signals backward through the network to determine which connections should change.
why: For people building AI, this would remove a major coordination requirement from training while preserving learning quality. Layers could become less dependent on one another’s update schedules, opening ways to keep data moving through a network as it learns.

sources.who: Timothy P. Lillicrap, Adam Santoro, Luke Marris, Colin J. Akerman and Geoffrey Hinton
sources.showed: They described how feedback in the brain might let individual connections approximate the learning signals used by backpropagation.
sources.cited_for: The review explains the biological motivation for learning from locally available signals.
sources.not_established: A proposed brain mechanism does not demonstrate competitive training of large artificial networks.

sources.showed: His Forward-Forward method trains each layer to distinguish real from negative examples without a backward pass. This preprint demonstrated learning on small problems.
sources.quote:
The forward-forward algorithm is somewhat slower than backpropagation and does not generalize
quite as well on several of the toy problems investigated in this paper so it is unlikely to replace
backpropagation for applications where power is not an issue.
sources.cited_for: A concrete learning method can operate without sending error signals backward through the whole network.
sources.not_established: The small demonstrations do not establish comparable learning as networks and training datasets grow.

sources.who: Zhaoxian Wu, Haichuan Liu and Tianyi Chen
sources.showed: Their preprint reports that tested local methods lagged behind backpropagation on image and language tasks. Several gaps grew with network depth or training scale.
sources.quote: This plateau arises because concurrent layer updates create a moving-target problem: an update in one layer changes the input distribution for the next layer, which is optimizing a different objective than it did at the previous step.
sources.cited_for: The tested methods expose difficulties in turning useful local changes into strong overall learning.
sources.not_established: These results do not prove that every possible local learning rule must fail.

shown: Hinton demonstrated local learning on small problems. Wu and colleagues tested several approaches at larger scales, reaching language models with 124 million adjustable connections, but reported substantial performance gaps. Both studies are preprints.
missing: A local rule still needs to match strong backpropagation training as model size, depth and training data grow.
A complete implementation needs to expose retained activity, delayed feedback and any dependence on repeated network-wide calculations.
Independent reproduction and full resource measurements are needed to establish that coordination burdens have actually been removed.
The same rule still needs a hardware demonstration measuring training energy alongside learning quality.

milestones.label: Comparable language learning with a billion adjustable connections
milestones.explanation: A local rule would have to meet the proposed prediction-error margin without retaining the full activity history for a backward pass or sending errors backward through all layers. This would establish parity at the target scale.

milestones.label: Sustained learning quality across increasing training scales
milestones.explanation: Comparisons would have to be specified before testing across sizes, depths and data budgets, reporting prediction-error scores and all extra training work. This would distinguish sustained parity from an isolated success.

milestones.label: Reproducible local updates with full resource costs
milestones.explanation: Independent teams would have to reproduce results from a fully specified rule, with memory, computation, communication and repeated-run variation measured. This would expose hidden coordination or costly repeated calculations.

milestones.label: Measured hardware training energy alongside learning quality
milestones.explanation: The same rule would have to train on non-digital hardware or hardware that computes within memory, reporting energy per unit of text and quality, including supporting work. This would establish the implementation’s energy cost.

uncertain: It remains unclear which feedback, memory and coordination dependencies should count as local learning.
The proposed performance margin and model-size threshold need justification; meeting them would not establish leading AI capabilities generally.
The reported failures may not extend to other local rules, and the costs of methods that repeatedly refine network activity remain unresolved.

page.title: Local learning with backpropagation parity
page.definition: One learning rule trains a deep network layer by layer or in groups of layers called blocks. Each block passes its output forward and updates its weights from its own objective. Gradients may flow within a block but stop at its boundary, so training requires no network-wide record of activations for a backward pass. The rule matches end-to-end backpropagation both in image classification with a linear classifier trained on frozen features and in next-token prediction at the specified language-model sizes.

goal.need: Teams that split a model across GPUs send activations forward and wait for gradients to travel back. Compression reduces traffic but leaves that wait. At equal prediction quality, local updates would let each GPU train its block as soon as it computes its own loss. In a 400M-class language model, peak memory fell from 29.2 GiB end to end to 14.5–15.8 GiB for the largest of four stages measured separately. Each stage still needed its input from the preceding stage, and the extra prediction heads added training computation.

completion.title: Independent investigators reproduce one local rule’s parity across the cited image and language comparisons.
completion.criterion: Independent investigators reproduce one rule using current-minibatch activities, targets and local parameter/optimizer state, with no task-error gradient crossing a layer or block boundary and no retained end-to-end backward graph. Under the cited image protocols, mean linear-readout accuracy reaches 80.69% on CIFAR-10, 81.97% on STL-10, 36.78% on Tiny ImageNet and 55.19% on ImageNet or better. On FineWeb-Edu, at equal token budgets, mean validation loss is at most 2.771 nats/token at step 5,000 for the 125M class and 2.418 at step 14,000 for the 400M class, each with both two and four equal-depth blocks. The rule also matches or improves on matched end-to-end reruns in every setting.
completion.set_by: Technology Atlas fallback, using published comparison settings; no external body was found that sets this combined test.
completion.basis: The Atlas combines the published image and language baselines with a zero mean performance deficit and independent reproduction. The image comparison uses an architecture-matched baseline below the state of the art. The language comparison matches training tokens and evaluation steps. Its auxiliary heads add computation, and the published quality comparisons use one seed. AlgoPerf scores time to target on separate workloads.

milestones.title: A locally trained network reaches at most 1.36% MNIST test error after 60 epochs.
milestones.criterion: Train four fully connected hidden layers of 2,000 rectified linear units each on MNIST with supervised Forward-Forward learning. Encode the label in the first ten input pixels, pairing each image with a correct label for positive examples and an incorrect label for negative examples. Reach at most 1.36% test error after 60 epochs under the unaugmented protocol in section 3.3.
milestones.set_by: Technology Atlas fallback, adopting Hinton’s reported demonstration as a reference result; Hinton did not designate it as a field milestone.
milestones.threshold_quote: 1.36% test errors on MNIST after 60 epochs.

milestones.title: Locally learned image features reach at least 80.69% CIFAR-10 linear-readout accuracy.
milestones.criterion: Train the six-layer VGG encoder on CIFAR-10 with local self-supervised objectives, using the Table 2 architecture and augmentations, batch size 128 and 300 training epochs. Freeze the encoder, average-pool each layer’s features and concatenate them to train a linear classifier on labeled training images. Mean test accuracy across four random seeds must reach at least 80.69%.
milestones.set_by: Technology Atlas fallback, adopting the published CIFAR-10 comparison; the authors did not designate this numerical result as a field milestone.

milestones.title: A four-block 400M-class language model comes within 0.062 nats/token of end-to-end training.
milestones.criterion: Train the 24-layer, 400M-class decoder-only Transformer on the FineWeb-Edu 10BT sample in sequences of 4,096 tokens. Use four equal-depth blocks with local objectives and stop gradients at each boundary. At step 14,000, evaluate held-out next-token negative log likelihood through the final block’s output head. The loss must be no more than 0.062 nats/token above the end-to-end reference of 2.418 nats/token.
milestones.set_by: Technology Atlas fallback, adopting Moon and colleagues’ reported Table 1 gap; the authors did not set it as a field milestone.

milestones.title: One local learning rule matches backpropagation across all the specified image and language settings.
milestones.criterion: In the originating laboratory, one rule satisfies every image and language quality comparison in the completion criterion, under its locality conditions and the cited architectures, data and budgets. Mean performance meets both the published numerical references and matched end-to-end baseline reruns in every setting. This is the combined demonstration immediately preceding independent reproduction.
milestones.set_by: Technology Atlas fallback; no external cross-domain milestone was found. The component comparison settings come from the cited papers.

milestones.title: A locally trained network distinguishes five digit patterns across shifts in position.
milestones.criterion: Use Fukushima’s three-stage neocognitron and the five digit patterns 0 through 4 in Figure 6a. Present each pattern 20 times with random shifts, using the local learning rule without class labels. For the positions in Figure 6a–c, each digit must activate the same single final-layer cell at every position, and different digits must activate different cells.
milestones.set_by: Technology Atlas, adopting Fukushima’s pattern-recognition demonstration as an early test. No external body sets it as a milestone.
milestones.threshold_quote: each stimulus pattern has become to elicit an output only from one of the C-cells of the last layer

milestones.title: A greedily trained VGG-11 reaches 88.0% top-five accuracy on supervised ImageNet.
milestones.criterion: Use the supervised VGG-11 comparison in Table 3 of Belilovsky and colleagues. Train successive convolutional layers with local auxiliary classifiers, freezing the previously trained layers. Under the paper’s VGG-11 training schedule, the single model must place the correct class among its five highest-scoring predictions on at least 88.0% of ImageNet evaluation images. Use the single-model column and exclude the ensemble.
milestones.set_by: Technology Atlas, adopting the end-to-end VGG-11 top-five accuracy in Table 3. No external body sets this number as a milestone.

No roadmap, programme or professional-society statement was found that judges parity across these image and language comparisons infeasible or unworthy of pursuit.

definition = "One learning rule trains a deep network layer by layer or in groups of layers called blocks. Each block passes its output forward and updates its weights from its own objective. Gradients may flow within a block but stop at its boundary, so training requires no network-wide record of activations for a backward pass. The rule matches end-to-end backpropagation both in image classification with a linear classifier trained on frozen features and in next-token prediction at the specified language-model sizes.". Reason: The definition now explains what passes between blocks, where gradients stop, and what parity measures in each task.

goal.need = "Teams that split a model across GPUs send activations forward and wait for gradients to travel back. Compression reduces traffic but leaves that wait. At equal prediction quality, local updates would let each GPU train its block as soon as it computes its own loss. In a 400M-class language model, peak memory fell from 29.2 GiB end to end to 14.5\u201315.8 GiB for the largest of four stages measured separately. Each stage still needed its input from the preceding stage, and the extra prediction heads added training computation.". Reason: The perplexity figures describe the quality gap but omit who faces the hardware constraint, its measured size, and the cost of reducing it.
